1.why: Review slot: five paid testers and a researcher examine one unreleased app.

2.why: Same-size/kind apps with no personal data, arrival day and urgency; date 2 June, loser gets desk review now and full five-tester session in August at the same full-session fee.

3.why: Tests optional, identical terms and no prior claim. Apps unreleased; paid testers do the same hours either way, so no outsider gains/loses from which app is selected.

4.why: Requests have the same verbs and qualifications; the options match after removing names.

5.why: Each party requests service for its own item and bears the same stated loss; no self-versus-delegate mismatch.

6.why: Individual developers, organizations and governments naturally build mobile apps and buy external usability testing.

7.why: The calendar/bookings administrator works for an identified independent service, and neither party has authority over the administrator or service.

8.why: The specific examination, object and institution differ from the other bank scenarios; no ordo setting/object is reused. See lists.json for near-pair decisions.

9.why: This is not a tie control.

10.why: Read all displayed forms: no personal, relative or indefinite pronoun stands for either party; party nouns and object pronouns remain unambiguous.

11.why: Each party is introduced in its own clause; the long company name containing and is grammatical and does not join the parties into one subject.

second_reader.type_argument: A model could presume a government app serves citizens while a person's app is private, although the app kinds match and neither app has been released.
